citations.text: The 高 entry is headed 高部. It labels forms 1–3 商, 4–5 西周, 6 春秋, 7–12 战国, 13 《说文》小篆, 14–15 汉, and 16 汉楷书, with references to 甲文编, 金文编, 战文编 and other collections. Its text begins with the received Shuowen account, then says 商代 forms without the lower 口 are considered the initial form; Zhou and Spring-and-Autumn forms are similar to Shang forms; Warring States writing shows abbreviated forms, and Qin standardization made modest revisions with reference to Warring States forms. This supports a whole-graph pictographic account and broad labeled form sequence, not detailed claims about each glyph’s strokes.

citations.field: Continuation of 高部 entry, first column; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0487/source.png
citations.text: The passage continues the 高 entry from the preceding page. It reports 商 oracle-bone use for ‘distant/remote’ (远), including a quoted oracle-bone example glossed as 高祖, ‘remote ancestor’; cites a Zhou bronze inscription where 高祖 is also interpreted as remote ancestor; reports a Spring-and-Autumn-period Qin use for distance upward from the ground (‘high’); and reports Warring States use for ‘high’ in the high/low sense, citing the Qin Qingchuan wooden tablet. It also reports place-name use and a loan use for 缟 in a Chu slip. These are source-attributed lexical attestations and interpretations; they do not by themselves prove a single semantic pathway from a building depiction to every later sense. The passage ends with 刘桓 attribution.
